corrections: 1. 'Main charitable entity types' still cites a non-existent 'NGO Act 2001; Department of Employment & Workplace Safety'. CSOs are governed by the Civil Society Organizations Act of Bhutan 2007 (amended 2022) and must register with the independent Civil Society Organizations Authority (CSOA) as a Public Benefit Organization or Mutual Benefit Organization. 2. Under the Act the CSOA has up to 6 months to decide an application, so the time can run past 16 weeks.

1. NGO registration is not run by an 'NGO Registration Committee (Ministry of Foreign Affairs)'. The de facto Ministry of Economy (NGO Directorate, ngo.gov.af) registers, supervises and coordinates both domestic and foreign NGOs. Foreign NGOs register as 'foreign organizations' established under foreign law. 2. 'Main charitable entity types' still cites 'Law on NGOs 2005' and a 'Hezb and Foundations Act'. Replace these with the de facto authorities' NGO law and procedure administered by the Ministry of Economy, as the Notes already say.

1. Associations are now governed by the Associations Act, Law No. 3/2022 (ratified 9 May 2022), which replaced the 2003 Associations Act. Registration is with the Registrar of Associations, who must decide within 30 days, or the association is deemed registered. 2. MIRA is the Maldives Inland Revenue Authority, not 'Maldives Investment and Regulatory Authority'. It grants charitable/tax-exempt approval, not trust registration. Key requirements should be rewritten accordingly.

1. Cite the governing law: incorporated trustees are registered under the Companies and Allied Matters Act 2020, Part F (ss. 823-850), at the CAC. 2. 'NCMM (Nigerian Committee on Foreign Non-Governmental Organizations)' is not an identifiable body. The real post-CAC layers are: SCUML (EFCC) registration, which is free and mandatory before banking; and, for international NGOs, registration with the National Planning Commission. No 'Ministry of Interior Operational Readiness Certificate' was found. 3. The Foreign Aid (Regulation...) Bill 2026 (SB.1034) is pending and not yet law.

1. Ghana has no 'Charities Act' or 'Ghana Charities Commission'. The Notes say a Charities Commission has operated since ~2021, which is wrong. NPO licensing is done by the Non-Profit Organisation Secretariat (Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection) under the NPOs Policy/Directive 2020. The NPO Bill (2026 version) is still pending. 2. 'Dept. of Social Welfare issues license' should read 'NPO Secretariat issues licence'.

1. 'Key local requirements' still cites 'Law n° 2022-443 of 15 Aug 2022 on OSCs'. The operative text is Ordonnance n° 2024-368 of 12 June 2024 on the organisation of civil society, which replaced Loi 60-315 of 1960. The National Assembly (March 2025) and the Senate (April 2025) adopted the bill ratifying it. Remove the 2022-443 reference.

1. 'Key local requirements' still cites 'Law n° 2015-04/PRB of 30 Jan 2016 on NGOs' and a declaration at the DAGC. The operative regime is Loi n° 2025-19 of 22 July 2025, which replaced the 1901 law and covers associations, foundations and national and foreign NGOs. Under Decree 2025-575 of 24 Sept 2025, declaration is exclusively online via service-public.bj into the Registre des Associations et des Fondations, effective 19 Dec 2025. 2. A receipt can take up to 60 days, so '2-6 weeks' is optimistic. Use roughly 2-10 weeks.

1. The 'Law n° 2000-17 of 11 Aug 2000 on NGOs' in Key local requirements could not be verified. Associations follow the 1901-law model (declaration at the Ministry of Territorial Administration). NGO status was governed by Décret 92-130, now replaced by Décret 2022-002/PR of 5 Jan 2022 on NGO-government cooperation. 2. Under a circular of 7 Oct 2024, foreign NGOs must get formal recognition of NGO status from the Ministry of Territorial Administration before signing partnership agreements. Organisations operating without authorisation had 6 months to regularise.

1. Loi 064-2015/CNT is no longer current. It was replaced by Loi n° 011-2025/ALT of 17 July 2025 on freedom of association (87 articles, promulgated by decree 2025-0959/PF of 23 July 2025). Update 'Main charitable entity types' and remove the Law 014/1997 reference. 2. The claimed '2018 constitutional amendment barring foreign-funded NGOs' is unsupported and should be deleted. The real risk is enforcement: on 15 Apr 2026 the government dissolved 118 organisations and suspended 1,056 under the new law.

1. 'Key local requirements' still cites repealed Law n° 2001-019. Cite Loi n° 04-038 of 5 Aug 2004 as amended by Ordonnance 2024-008 (March 2024), which imposes prior authorization and declaration on all associations.

1. 'Key local requirements' still cites 'Law L/2010/004'. The operative texts are Loi L/2005/013/AN (associations/ONG). Loi L/2005/014 concerns cooperatives, not associations. 2. In Sept 2024 the MATD suspended the issuing of agréments to NGOs and associations for 4 months, and approvals have been irregular since. '4-10 weeks' is optimistic; flag that suspensions are possible.

1. 'Key local requirements' cites 'Lei n.º 5/VI/96', which uses Cape Verde-style numbering and is not a Guinea-Bissau text. The Notes also cite 'Loi L/005/013/AN (2013)', which is Guinea (Conakry) law. Delete both. The mechanism is a notarial public deed under the Código Civil (10+ founders) plus registry at the Conservatória, as the row's verified note says.

1. 'Loi n° 71-604 du 20 juillet 1971' is not the Senegalese associations law. Associations are governed by the Code des obligations civiles et commerciales, arts. 811 ff. (Loi 68-08 of 26 March 1968, amended by Loi 79-02), and Décret 76-040 of 16 Jan 1976. Art. 812 sets the rule: declaration plus registration, and registration can be refused only on legality grounds. 2. The declaration is filed with the administrative authority (Ministry of Interior/préfecture), not the 'Direction de l'Action Sociale (1965 decree)'. 3. The ONG decree citation (96-103 as amended by 2010-1490) is correct.

1. The NGO Decree is No. 81 of 1996, not 1993. It created the NGO Affairs Agency, which issues clearance certificates before incorporation. 2. The company route is under the Companies Act 2013, which replaced the 'Companies Act 1964/1955'. Charitable bodies register with the Registrar of Companies (CLG or registered association). The 'Societies Act 1972' was not confirmed as the operative route.

1. The Notes cite 'Companies Act 2013'. The governing law is the Companies Act 2009 (Act No. 5), as amended in 2014. 2. Besides CAC incorporation, NGOs must register with the government NGO regulator (Ministry of Planning/Finance & Economic Development NGO Regulations). That registration costs about US$500 plus an application form and SLANGO membership, and is renewed yearly. The ~$20 CAC fee understates the official cost of operating as an NGO.

1. No 'NGO Act of 2015 (Act No. 11 of 2015)' could be verified. NGOs are accredited under the National Aid & NGO Policy by the NGO Unit of the Ministry of Finance and Development Planning, which runs an online platform since Aug 2022. This follows incorporation at the Liberia Business Registry and Ministry of Foreign Affairs endorsement. 2. The US$150 accreditation fee applies to local NGOs. International NGOs pay US$350, plus annual fees of US$100 (international) or US$50 (local). The '3-year renewal' claim is unverified.

1. 'Key local requirements' and Notes cite 'Law 93-010', which could not be verified. The association regime is Ordonnance 84-06 of 1 March 1984, amended by Ord. 84-50 and Loi 91-006. It requires declaration and prior authorization. NGOs fall under Décret 2022-182. 2. Add the 2025-26 crackdown: the Interior Ministry suspended about 2,900 NGOs and associations in 2025, and an arrêté of 7 Jan 2026 dissolved many, leaving about 1,809 authorised.
